descriptionChirho: The nominal sense of lat meaning 'secret arts, enchantments' — hidden magical practices used by sorcerers and magicians; Arabic سِحْر (sihr) 'sorcery/magic'; Korean 비법들 (bibeopdeul) 'secret methods/arts'; Spanish encantamientos 'enchantments'; Hindi जादू (jaadoo) 'magic/sorcery'; Swahili uchawi 'witchcraft/sorcery.' All 3 occurrences appear in the Exodus plague narratives (Ex 7:11,22; 8:3,14 [Heb 8:3,14]) where Pharaoh's magicians replicate Moses' signs 'with their secret arts' (be-lateihem). The construct with possessive suffix (their enchantments) and the prepositional frame (by means of) characterize this as a technical term for occult magical practice, distinct from the general adverbial sense of secrecy.

The adverbial/nominal sense of lat meaning 'secretly, in secret' — describing actions done covertly or in a hidden manner, without occult connotation; Arabic سِرًّا (sirran) 'secretly' and خُفْيَة (khufya) 'concealment/secrecy'; Korean 은밀히 (eunmilhi) 'secretly' and 몰래 (mollae) 'stealthily'; Spanish en secreto 'in secret'; Hindi चुपके से (chupke se) 'quietly/stealthily'; Swahili kimya kimya 'quietly/secretly' and kwa siri 'in secret.' All 3 occurrences use lat in a prepositional phrase (be-lat, ha-lat) to describe covert human action — bringing something secretly (Judg 4:21; Ruth 3:7; 1 Sam 18:22) — without any magical or sorcerous connotation. Distinguished from the 'enchantments' sense by describing ordinary human concealment rather than occult practice.
